html:
"Sasanian dependencies" is the map's label for Yemen in 600 and 700, when it was a province of the Persian Sasanian Empire, from about 570 to 628.

Before that, Yemen had been the kingdom of Himyar, then fell to Christian invaders from Aksum in the 520s; their general Abraha ruled as king. A Yemeni noble, Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan, asked Persia for help, and Khosrow I sent a small force under the commander Wahriz, which drove the Ethiopians out around 570. Persian governors then ruled from Sanaa, and their descendants in Yemen were called the Abna, "the sons".

In 628 the governor Badhan accepted Islam, and Yemen passed into the new Muslim state of Muhammad. The map keeps the label in 700, after Persian rule had ended.
sum: "Sasanian dependencies" is the map's label for Yemen in 600 and 700, when it was a province of the Persian Sasanian Empire, from about 570 to 628.
